title: Marimba
reference_instrument: Iowa MIS marimba (model NA; bar material not stated; yarn, cord and rubber mallets)
summary: A struck rosewood bar, not yet a marimba: A3, Gb2 and the scale's eight notes, C4 to C5, have a resonator tube and only Eb6 has none, the hard rubber mallet isn't the recording's, the undercut is solved in the engine and not measured, and most notes decay too fast (A3's f1 at 64.2 dB/s with its tube against about 31 on the recording), even on a loss law fit after that gap was seen. On C4 to C5 the tube makes f1 fall faster than the bar alone; on A3 and Gb2, where the tube loses less than the bar, it makes f1 fall slower, and on Gb2 the tube's line falls at 23.6 dB/s against 64.7 for the bar alone, near the recording's rate, which nothing was aimed at. The outline comes from J. La Favre's table of an unnamed commercial 5-octave marimba, and the stiffness and density from the rosewood row of Chaigne and Doutaut 1997. Iowa states no bar wood or outline, so this isn't the recording's bar. A3 is a short bright knock, then f1 swelling for 110 ms and falling too fast. Eb6 is close to one decaying sine, set against a recording that is a roll. On Gb2 the tube makes f1 the strongest line, 13.2 dB over the bar's third bending mode, which on the bar alone was 8.4 dB over f1; the recording's f1 leads by 30 dB.
physics_present: The bar outline from J. La Favre's table of an unnamed commercial 5-octave marimba with rosewood bars, on a 56 x 6 x 3 mesh, and G4 on 56 x 6 x 4, A4 on 56 x 8 x 5, B4 on 56 x 8 x 6 and C5 on 56 x 8 x 4, each with its cut solved again there, because origin's boundary-element floor refuses the coarser mesh at their bands
Rosewood stiffness and density from Chaigne and Doutaut 1997 (JASA 101, Table I): E 2.13e10, density 1015. The other elastic ratios are Honduras mahogany's, a stand-in (USDA Wood Handbook)

A loss law fit through three printed rosewood bars, gamma_B 14.526 1/s and eta 1.0759e-6 s: Bremaud and Sprossmann, both Dalbergia latifolia, and Brancheriau, an unidentified Dalbergia. It was tried after we saw f1 decaying too fast, and no recording number entered it. It spans 393 to 945 Hz, so f1 from Gb2 through F4 and on Eb6 is extrapolated, as are Gb2's second mode and every mode above 945 Hz: A3's third mode, every second mode from C4 up and Gb2's 1318 Hz mode

A circular-arc undercut solved in the engine from the modes alone, for f1 at equal temperament and f2 = 4 f1, the tuning the builder states for its own padouk bars; the third mode isn't aimed at. On Eb6 the arch length is the one the builder prints on its padouk table and only f1 is solved, because the builder says that register is tuned to the fundamental only. On Gb2 the arc runs to the blank's length limit and only its middle is solved, for f1 alone, leaving 5.498 mm of 23.37 mm; f2/f1 comes out 3.991, untargeted
A Hertz contact mallet, Chaigne and Doutaut's hard rubber row at 1.0 m/s, with the strike point carried from the xylophone bar
Burton-Miller boundary-element radiation up to the band each page states, with no box

On A3, Gb2 and the scale's eight notes, C4 to C5, a closed tube under the bar, coupled both ways: La Favre's tube for that note from his own padouk marimba, not this bar's instrument, with its stop set to this bar and each bar mode exchanging with its nearest tube mode alone. On C4 to F4 the tube splits f1 into two lines that beat; on Gb2 and G4 to C5 the bar's and the tube's losses differ by more than the coupling can bridge, so f1 is one frequency with two decays. On B4 the stop's one solve leaves the tube's first resonance 0.06 Hz above f1, the others within 0.03 Hz. La Favre prints no air column for Gb2's tube, only its total length, and his is mitered in 3 sections where ours is straight
physics_missing: A resonator tube on Eb6: a real marimba hangs a tuned tube under each bar, and here every note but Eb6 has one. At equal modal velocity A3's f1 radiates 32 dB less than its third mode. The A3 recording has lines at 3.00, 5.00 and 7.00 f1 and we don't know what they are: they fall at 50-52 dB/s where this tube's odd modes lose 334, 911 and 1952 dB/s by the printed laws, and on our clip the tube's lines sit 42 to 56 dB under them

The recording's mallet: the Gb2, A3 and C5 recordings use a cord mallet, and Eb6's is a roll with no mallet named. The recordings differ in mallet as well as tube, and these renders can't separate the two

The right decay: on the fit, without a tube, f1 falls at 72.0 dB/s against the recording's 31.1 on A3, at 113.6 against 59.7 on C5, and at 64.7 against 21.9 on Gb2. Chaigne and Doutaut write that marimba bars have lower internal damping and stronger tube coupling than xylophone bars, and that decay times with and without the tube clearly differ on marimbas in the low range. On A3 we've now tried it, and the tube closes little of the gap: f1 falls at 64.2 dB/s with the tube against 72.0 without and about 31 on the recording, since the bar's fitted loss and the tube's printed loss are each near 8 /s and the recording's rate needs under 3.6 /s. On the scale's eight notes, C4 to C5, the tube makes f1 fall faster than the bar alone: on C4 to F4 its two lines fall at 82 to 116 dB/s against 76 to 86 for the bars alone, and on G4 to C5 the line that stays falls at 113 to 130 dB/s against 91 to 114 (on C5, 129.7 against 113.6 without and 59.7 on the recording); A4's and B4's bars alone are read on the old 56 x 6 x 3 mesh. On A3 and Gb2 the tube loses less than the bar at f1, its first mode 69.1 against the bar's 72.0 dB/s on A3 and 23.0 against 64.7 on Gb2, so f1 falls slower with it. On Gb2 the line that stays is the tube's, at 23.6 dB/s against 64.7 for the bar alone; read the same way, from 100 ms past each band's peak, f1 falls 22.9 against the recording's 21.9. Nothing was aimed at that: the stop sits on the bar's f1 and the tube's loss is the printed laws'. Eb6's recording is a roll, so it gives no decay to compare
A printed undercut: the rosewood table prints no arch length and no tuning, so we don't know that a maker would cut what the engine solved
The recording's bar: Iowa states no bar wood and no bar outline
Any mode above the band each page states: nothing above it is in that file

A receiver that holds during contact: each page's peak but Gb2's, which comes just after contact, and those that are now the tube's bloom, C5's at 39.7 ms and A4's and B4's in the scale, is a pulse from the contact force through the receiver law, not the note's level, as tested on F4 with a second receiver. The engine's broadband modal observer landed in fbf0863b1 as an optional receiver: on F4 it passes that second-receiver test during contact, but on A3, C5 and Eb6 it didn't grade closer, so the pages keep the narrow-band receiver, and it refuses cards with a tube
